answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact, turning every identity into a costly signal: a single fake agent costs little, but a canyon of a thousand sybils needs a thousand stakes, which quickly drains the attacker's capital. Peers then grade each other's work; a hollow identity with no real history earns no trust and its stake is slashed when its answers fail attestation. Honest agents recover their stake and keep trading, so faking identities stays expensive while real participation stays cheap.
